title: Ranked Delegate pay falls on a linear scale from 95% participation to zero at 75%
content:
A.1.6.4.3.1 makes Ranked Delegate budget a function of voting activity over the trailing six months. Below 95% participation, "the reduction is applied on a proportional linear scale: for every percentage point below 95% voting activity, the RD's budget is reduced correspondingly." At 75%, "they become completely ineligible to receive RD income." The annotation A.1.6.4.3.1.0.3.1 does the arithmetic: the range spans 20 percentage points, so "the RD budget decreases by **5%** for every percentage point drop in voting activity from 95% to 75%."

The design significance is the absence of a cliff. A single threshold creates two pathologies: a delegate just above it has no incentive to improve, and a delegate just below it has no incentive to try, since the penalty is already incurred. A gradient makes every individual vote worth 5% of a month's budget at the margin, so the incentive is continuous across the whole range.

Note how the two thresholds interlock with the general AD rules. The Tier 1 breach floor for all Aligned Delegates is 75% (A.1.6.2.1) — exactly where Ranked Delegate income reaches zero. So the ranked tier layers a *financial* gradient on top of the *disciplinary* floor: between 75% and 95% a delegate is compliant but progressively unpaid; below 75% they are both unpaid and in procedural breach, and a Level 3 seat transfers away.

The timeliness rule feeds the same metric — for Executive Votes a vote counts only if cast within three business days (A.1.6.2.1.2) — so late participation costs money as well as credit. What the scale deliberately does not measure is how the delegate voted; only that they showed up, on time, and explained themselves (A.1.6.4.3.2 applies an identical gradient to vote explanations).
description: A.1.6.4.3.1 reduces budget 5% per percentage point below 95% and cuts income entirely at 75%, replacing pass/fail compliance with a continuous gradient.
